name: The Eighth Summer
summary: The Hounders scour the Chalk Hound every seventh summer so that it stays asleep. This is the eighth, and the scour-mistress will not call them out until she knows what is at the bottom of her husband's cord in the Hound's Swallet.
notes: Hearthvale world life, the region's large site. Links the Scourers' Lodge, the Chalk Hound and the Hound's Swallet (a cave delve, core:interior/hounds_swallet) and its boss, the Old Hound.

stages.journal: Tamsin Hounder will not call the scourers out until she knows what is at the bottom of her husband's cord. First she wants somebody to look at the Chalk Hound itself: to lie in its eye, where the scourers sing it shut, and see how far the turf has crept in since the last scouring.

objectives.text: Lie in the Chalk Hound's eye

stages.journal: The turf has come a hand's breadth into the Hound's eye, green on the white, and from inside the eye the whole south flank of the down is in view, and the dark of the swallet on it. Seven years ago Aldous Hounder went down there after a wolf, tied on to the lodge gate by a scourer's cord. The cord is still taut.

objectives.text: Go to the Hound's Swallet on the south flank of Hound Down
Follow the white cord down to what holds it
Take up Aldous Hounder's cord

stages.journal: The cord ended at a rake-head worn to a stub, in the deepest chamber of the swallet, under the great grey-gold thing that had been lying on it. Tamsin Hounder is waiting at the lodge gate with seventy-one white cords.

objectives.text: Tell Tamsin Hounder what to do about the eighth summer

options.text: Call the scourers out.
Let the turf have the eye.
Tie Aldous's cord on the gate as the seventy-second scouring.

name: The Hurdwell Bell
summary: A family whose line has ended has its bell buried at the foot of the Brow's Long Table. This spring the Hurdwell bell was dug up, and the boot-print beside the hole was a Larkbourne boot.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Brow Long Table and Hanging Coombe, where the Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang hang stolen bells in the trees.

stages.journal: The Table-Warden thinks the Hurdwell bell went to Hanging Coombe, in the hollow of Rook Wood, where the Larkbourne Boys' eastern gang hang the boundary-bells they steal from the Vale's hawthorns. A small bronze bell, green from the ground, HURDWELL cut round its shoulder.

objectives.text: Go to Hanging Coombe
Deal with the bell-thieves
Find the Hurdwell bell among the stolen ones

stages.journal: Among the boundary-bells in the coombe's trees, one that never hung on a hawthorn: green from the ground, and flat when it rings. Oswen Bellsey has changed his mind every evening about where it should go.

objectives.text: Tell Oswen Bellsey where the Hurdwell bell belongs

options.text: Bury it again at the table's foot.
Hang it at the table's head.
Bury it, and ring it for the Larkbourne Boys too.

name: A Furrow Further Off
summary: Every spring the Lime Bay Kilns send fourteen bushel of quicklime south to Ashway to lime the headland on the grey side. This spring the cart has not gone, and Rab Ashway has found the grey lying in his last furrow.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Lime Bay Kilns and Ashway Farm, the length of the Vale from the Mere shore to the grey's edge.

stages.journal: Hedda Limeburner's son will not take the south cart past the Hare and Hurdle since a bristleback came at it. The first sack is the one that matters: the headland first, then the field.

objectives.text: Take the sack with the red cord from Hedda

stages.journal: A double sack of quicklime tied with Hedda's red cord, warm through the sacking. Rab Ashway farms the southernmost fields in the Vale, down past the Hare and Hurdle where the country stops being green.

objectives.text: Give Rab Ashway his lime

stages.journal: Rab Ashway took the sack without a word and carried it to the headland himself, and stood in the grey furrow with a shovel for a long time. Hedda Limeburner will want to know it arrived.

objectives.text: Tell Hedda the lime reached Ashway

name: Nine Couple of Hounds
summary: The Wardens' Rest's pack of hounds, nine couple bred from a line older than the Rest, went over the kennel wall at midnight without one of them giving tongue. The kennel-master chained the gate behind them from outside.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Wardens' Kennels, the Warden Barrow and Wolf Holt.

stages.journal: The Rest's Wardens saw the pack the first night lying round the kerb of the Warden Barrow, where the first Wardens are buried with their nine hand-bells. Garrick Coupler wants to know what they left there.

objectives.text: Go to the Warden Barrow
Find what the pack left on the kerb

stages.journal: A hound-couple on the barrow's kerb, the collars unbuckled, not broken: somebody let two hounds out of their couple on purpose. The calling came from the west, from Wolf Holt, where the down-wolves took back the Fallowfold shepherds' flint fold.

objectives.text: Go to Wolf Holt
Drive off the wolves at the Holt
Find Bellmouth's collar

stages.journal: Bellmouth's collar, in the Holt among the wolves' bones and the hounds' tracks, her bell stopped with a twist of grass so the pack could not hear her. Garrick Coupler is sitting by his chained gate.

objectives.text: Tell Garrick Coupler what to do about the kennel

options.text: Take off the chain and leave the gate open.
Breed a new pack from the Rest's pups.
Let Pim call them home by name.

name: What the Brow Sings
summary: On still nights the Brow sings, a few bars at a time, from nowhere. The Wardens' Listener writes the verses down because the Roll says Larkstead was known for its singing, and that they stopped. Three pages of her book are blank.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Listener's Shieling, the Hush Steps, the Hushwatch stones and the Cliff Graves.

stages.journal: The singing is loudest in three places the Listener can no longer bring herself to go at night: the last of the Hush Steps down the cliff face, between the Hushwatch stones, and among the cliff graves above Rookdown. The Listener before her left a slate at each for whoever heard a verse there.

objectives.text: Take up the slate on the last of the Hush Steps
Take up the slate between the Hushwatch stones
Take up the slate at the Cliff Graves

stages.journal: Three slates, three verses, in three hands the Wardens do not know, one of them a child's. They are not about the Brow. They are about being listened to.

objectives.text: Tell Linnet Crale what to do with the verses

options.text: Send them to the Rest for the Roll.
Sing them back from the Brow.
Keep them in her book.

name: The Other Ink
summary: Five carters who would not pay the Scathe tithe are buried on the down in sight of the fort, each under his wheel. Captain Wendle wrote down what was done to each of them, in a different ink. The widow of one of them wants the book.
notes: Hearthvale world life. Links the Wheel Graves and Scathe Fort (0-C's showcase); runs beside The Scathe Tithe, which takes the same book to the Rest, and does not take it off you.

stages.journal: Captain Hobb Wendle keeps his tithe book in the undercroft under Scathe's keep, where the Wardens kept theirs, and the carters who would not pay are written in it in another ink. He will not hand it over.

objectives.text: Deal with Captain Hobb Wendle
Take his tithe book

stages.journal: Wendle's book, the carters who paid in a careful hand and the ones who would not in another ink, with what was done. Bel Axtree asked for it to come to the graves first.

objectives.text: Tell Bel Axtree what to do with the other ink

options.text: Read the other ink aloud at the graves.
Burn it unread.
Send it to the Wardens' Rest.

name: The Night Shift
summary: Nell Knapper keeps a lantern lit at the head of Knappers' Deep for the night shift the roof came down on eleven winters ago, and every night something under Hound Down knocks the overman's count. The Larkbourne Boys dig her floorstone in the upper galleries; past the Fall is her father.
notes: Hearthvale world life phase 2, a large site. Knappers' Deep (delve with its own builder: headframe, gin, spoil) and its mine inside, core:interior/knappers_deep; the Boys' ganger (a Larkbourne Bruiser in the first gallery) and the Gaffer at the far face.

stages.journal: Nell Knapper wants the Larkbourne Boys out of her galleries before anything else: they have a camp in the first gallery under the shaft, and a big lad who does their talking. The ladder goes down from the headframe on the lip of Hound Down.

objectives.text: Go down the ladder at Knappers' Deep
Turn the Boys' ganger out of the first gallery

stages.journal: The Boys dug along the seam round the Fall, and there is a way through it now that the Vale never had. Past it are the night shift's galleries. Nell wants her father's tally: an overman counts his shift up the ladder, and somebody has to finish the count.

objectives.text: Go past the Fall to the far face
Take the overman's tally

stages.journal: The tally-stick has eight notches. The knocking under Hound Down has stopped. Nell Knapper is at the shaft head with her lantern, waiting to hear what is to be done with the Deep.

objectives.text: Tell Nell Knapper what is to be done with the Deep

options.text: Cap the shaft.
Work the Deep again.
Bring the shift up to the hedge line.

name: The Stone's Note
summary: The Hum Stone on the lip of the Brow has hummed with the Toll since the spring, and Merrowby's bellwright says every band of bronze the barrow-diggers cut off it cracks one of Merrowby's family bells. The diggers went down a door of the Builders' under the stone, and the Hush's dead went down after them.
notes: Hearthvale world life phase 2, a large site. The Hum Stone (delve with its own builder: the monolith, its hump and the Builders' door) and the vaults under it, core:interior/hum_stone_throat; the barrow-diggers, the Hush's dead come up after the hum, and Dunstan Spade at the bottom.

stages.journal: Godwin Merrow, Merrowby's bellwright, is camped on the Brow's lip by the Hum Stone with his tuning bells. The barrow-diggers have cut two bands of the stone's bronze and gone down a door of the Builders' under it, and their king, Dunstan Spade, has the crown band. Nobody has come up for a fortnight.

objectives.text: Go down the Builders' door under the Hum Stone
Find Dunstan Spade at the bottom of the throat
Take back the stone's crown band

stages.journal: The crown band rings when it is knocked, and something a long way off rings back. Godwin Merrow is at his bell frame on the lip, waiting to hear what is to be done with it.

objectives.text: Tell Godwin Merrow what is to be done with the crown band

options.text: Hang it back on the stone.
Cast an eighteenth bell for Merrowby.
Bury it and let the stone go quiet.

name: The Long Wake
summary: Wake Barrow on Hound Down has had a lamp in its forecourt every night since the Ash Winter, when the last barrow-wife, Ebba Crowle, went down to sit with that winter's dead. Since midsummer the lamp goes out every night, and the stone that sealed the barrow is walking out of its socket.
notes: Hearthvale world life phase 2, the third large site. Wake Barrow (delve with its own builder: the long mound, the Wake Oaks, the façade and the walked-out stone) and the crypt under it, core:interior/wake_barrow_crypt; the wakeless (the Ash Winter's dead), down wolves come in by the oak's root, and Ebba Crowle at the bottom.

stages.journal: Tamsin Crowle keeps the lamp at Wake Barrow on Hound Down. It has gone out every night since midsummer, and the great stone that sealed the barrow in the Ash Winter has walked out of its socket far enough to get by. Ebba Crowle, the last barrow-wife, went down with her lamp and the winter's dead two hundred years ago. Tamsin wants the lamp brought up.

objectives.text: Go into Wake Barrow past the stone
Find whoever is sitting the wake at the bottom
Take up Ebba Crowle's lamp

stages.journal: Ebba Crowle's lamp is cold, and its handle is still warm. Tamsin Crowle is at the forecourt niche, waiting to hear what is to be done with it.

objectives.text: Tell Tamsin Crowle what is to be done with the lamp

options.text: Light it again by her, and let the stone go back.
Take her to the Wardens and the Roll.
Keep it lit in the niche, and sit her wake up here.

name: The Last Wassail
summary: Forty winters ago the last Wassail King of the Great Press, Hob Applegarth, would not give back his crown at dawn, and was barred in the cellars under Wassail Knap with his wassailers. This spring the dead orchard over the cellars blossomed at midnight, singing comes up through the grates, and three Hazelcombe pickers have followed it down.
notes: Hearthvale novel round: the large site. Wassail Knap (delve, builder wassail_knap: the press-house, the press-beam and screw, the dead orchard, the Wassail Tree) and the cellars under it, core:interior/wassail_cellars (keep); the wassailers, the King's table, Hob Applegarth at the Mother Vat. Leads out: the crown goes to the Mother Pippin by Tamwick, a choice at the tree.

stages.journal: Three Hazelcombe pickers followed the singing down the cellar stair at Wassail Knap and have not come up; Pip Applegarth wants to know what has them. She keeps watch from her hut at the orchard's edge, and she will not go down herself: she is an Applegarth, and the King down there is her grandfather.

objectives.text: Go down the cellar stair at Wassail Knap
Find what became of the Hazelcombe pickers

stages.journal: The pickers' tally-stick lay in the wassail hall under the dancers' feet, and the pickers are dancing; the King who keeps the revel going sits at the Mother Vat below. Pip said that if anybody got the crown off him the singing would stop, and everybody in it could go home.

objectives.text: Go down to the Mother Vat and stop the Wassail King
Take the Wassail Crown

stages.journal: Pip Applegarth said the crown was cut from the Mother Pippin's withies and must go back to her, not to any Applegarth. The old tree stands in its own field south of Tamwick. What is done with a King's crown at her roots is for whoever took it off him to say.

objectives.text: Give the Wassail Crown back to the Mother Pippin

options.text: Hang the crown in her branches, and let her orchards wake.
Bury the crown at her roots, and let the old orchards go to sleep.
Carry it to Tamwick, for a new King to wear one night and give back at dawn.

stages.journal: The crown has gone back and the knap is quiet; Pip Applegarth is at her hut by the cellar-head, waiting to hear the singing has stopped for good.

objectives.text: Tell Pip Applegarth what was done with the crown

name: The Forty-First
summary: Abner Strawe has stood forty scarecrows on the Moot on Hound Down, each from a farm he can name. This summer there are forty-one, and the rooks will not sit on one of them.
notes: Hearthvale novel round: the Scarecrow Moot (kind scarecrow_moot, builder scarecrow_moot). The forty-first is a hedge-wight stood asleep in the ranks at odd_rank; looking it in the face (the touch TheOddOne) or striking it wakes it (encounters/pois_hearthvale.json).

stages.journal: Abner Strawe set forty scarecrows on the Moot and now counts forty-one, and the rooks will not sit on the one at the end of the third rank. He has asked you to find the one that is not a scarecrow.

objectives.text: Find the one in the ranks that is not a scarecrow, and put it down

stages.journal: The forty-first was a hedge-wight stood in the ranks in a dead farmer's coat; Abner Strawe will want to know it is down, and to count his forty again.

objectives.text: Tell Abner Strawe the Moot is forty again

name: The Third Hand
summary: Somebody who is neither of Briarfoot's two Wardens chalks warnings on the tower's tally-board: that the grey is coming to the tower, not the Stone, and to ask who is on the terraces at midnight.
notes: Hearthvale novel round: the quest Briarfoot Watch (a large site of phase 1) had none of. The thing at midnight is the encounter's hedge-wight; Amis Hale's bell lies at the tally-board; leads out to the Candle-Wheel, where Amis Hale's is the Roll candle that keeps going out.

stages.journal: A third hand chalks warnings on Briarfoot's tally-board and Warden Oakden wants to know whose; it says to ask who is on the terraces at midnight.

objectives.text: Be at the foot of Briarfoot Watch at midnight, and meet what comes up from the grey
Look at what lies under the tally-board

stages.journal: A Warden's bell lay under the tally-board, AMIS HALE, BRIARFOOT scratched round its lip; Warden Oakden keeps the Roll's copy and will know the name. There is chalk ground into the scratches.

objectives.text: Show Warden Oakden the bell

stages.journal: Amis Hale is not on Briarfoot's copy of the Roll, so Warden Oakden asks you to take her name to the Candle-Wheel, where a candle burns for every name on it. The bell is a Warden's; the Roll let her go.

objectives.text: Give Amis Hale's name to Tallis Dipper at the Candle-Wheel

options.text: Dip her a candle and set it on the Roll shelf, where the one that keeps going out was.
Send her name to the Rest with the next Roll candles, to be written in the Roll itself.

name: Counted Out
summary: Enid Drove counts her ewes in twice every evening and the second count is one more. She was a drover's girl the night the Briar shut its gate, and the flock her father penned in the Drovers' Pound that night was never counted out.
notes: Hearthvale novel round: the quest the Drovers' Pound (a large site of phase 1) had none of. The tally lies in the pound (its encounter's `lies`), under the wolves; leads out to Enid Drove at the Bram Down Wheelhouse with it.

stages.journal: Enid Drove thinks her extra ewe is from the last flock the Drovers' Pound held, never counted out; she wants the drovers' tally-board brought out of the pound.

objectives.text: Clear the down wolves out of the Drovers' Pound
Take the drovers' tally-board from inside the gate

stages.journal: The tally has the last flock counted into the pound the night the gate shut and no line for the morning; Enid Drove wants to be there when it is settled.

objectives.text: Bring the tally to Enid Drove at her wheelhouse

options.text: Count them out, with her, and burn the line in under the last one.
Leave them counted in. The down has kept them this long.

name: The Last Sheaf
summary: The Great Barn at Southgate held the East Downs' last harvest the year the Briar shut, and the kern-baby plaited from its last sheaf was never carried out in spring. This summer men of straw walk out of the old ricks at dusk and cut Southgate's barley green.
notes: Hearthvale novel round: the second large site. The Great Barn (delve, builder great_barn: the crucks, the gables, the porch, the ricks) and the undercroft, core:interior/great_barn_undercroft (ruined_hall); sheaf-men, reapers, bristlebacks, and the Kern Mother. Leads out: the kern-knot goes to the Brow Long Table, a choice at the table.

stages.journal: Somebody is cutting Southgate's barley green at night and standing it up facing the Great Barn; Dunnock Southgate wants to know what is down in its undercroft. His grandfather, the last tithe-reeve, burned everything into his tally, and kept it in the tithe vault.

objectives.text: Go down the stair at the Great Barn
Find the tithe-reeve's last tally

stages.journal: The reeve's tally hung the kern-baby on the tie-beam for Plough Monday and has no mark for Plough Monday; what brings the harvest in hangs in the sheaf hall. Dunnock said she only ever wanted carrying out.

objectives.text: Go down to the sheaf hall and cut down the Kern Mother
Take up the kern-knot from her straw

stages.journal: The kern-knot is fifty harvests late and still warm; the Brow keeps its harvest at the Long Table, and that is where a last sheaf is owed. Oswen Bellsey, the Table-Warden, will want to hear it from whoever carried it out.

objectives.text: Carry the kern-knot to Oswen Bellsey at the Brow Long Table

options.text: Set it at the head of the Long Table, and let the Brow keep its harvest supper.
Carry it back to Southgate, to be ploughed into the first furrow as it should have been.
Burn it on the Brow, and let fifty years' harvest go.

stages.journal: The last sheaf has been seen to and nothing should be cutting Southgate's barley now; Dunnock Southgate is at the Great Barn, watching his top field to be sure.

objectives.text: Tell Dunnock Southgate the last sheaf has been seen to
